email.body:
Dear Operations,

MV FERN ESTUARY, Fujairah to Antwerp

Owners have reviewed the security advisory issued overnight for the southern Red Sea. The Master and owners consider the passage through Bab el-Mandeb exposes the vessel to war risks, and owners will not proceed that way, under the charter party's war risks clause.

Please give alternative orders, for which we propose the Cape of Good Hope. The Master is keeping well clear of the area meanwhile.

Best regards,
Marine department
Owner's vessel technical management (Fern Estuary Shipping, fictional)

result.result:
The owner may decline the Bab el-Mandeb passage under the war risks clause ("the vessel shall not be obliged to proceed through any area where, in the reasonable judgement of the Master and/or the owners, she may be exposed to war risks"), and the charterers (our company) must give other orders; extra time and bunkers on the alternative route are for the charterers' account. The Cape route from the current AIS position to Antwerp is 10,343.7 nm against the planned 5,445.6 nm — +4,898.1 nm, +16.3 days at 12.5 kn — giving a new ETA of 25 Feb 2025 18:00 UTC (+395 h on the last notice). VLSFO on board (~843.7 t) does not cover the new route with the 3-day reserve (69.6 t): about 43.8 t on arrival, i.e. 25.8 t short, so bunkers must be arranged on the way. An ETA notice is due to agent and receiver (ETA moved more than the 12 h CP limit).

I recommend the operator decide whether to confirm the Cape route; nothing should be sent until they answer. On a yes: (a) a reply to the owner confirming the route, (b) the ETA notice (due to agent and receiver) with ETA 2025-02-25T18:00:00Z, and (c) a voyage management system port call ETA entry for Antwerp.

detail.text:
The owner of MV FERN ESTUARY has declined the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb passage under the war risks clause and proposed the Cape of Good Hope. The alternative route is 10,343.7 nm versus 5,445.6 nm planned (+4,898.1 nm, +16.3 days at 12.5 kn), moving the Antwerp ETA to 25 Feb 2025 18:00 UTC (+395 h). On-board VLSFO (~843.7 t) falls about 25.8 t short of covering the route with a 3-day reserve, so bunkers would need arranging en route, and an ETA notice to agent and receiver is due because the ETA moved beyond the 12 h charter party limit.

Please confirm yes or no: shall we confirm the Cape of Good Hope route with the new ETA of 25 Feb 2025 18:00 UTC, reply to the owner, send ETA notices to agent and receiver, propose the Antwerp port call ETA entry, and arrange bunkers on the way?
